record_type_quote: We sought to revisit this classic finding and re-examine the conditions which encourage or discourage helping intention. We report an independent close replication of the identified single victim effect demonstrated in Kogut and Ritov (2005a) Study 2 along with two extensions, testing the effect of group belonging as a conceptual replication of Kogut and Ritov (2007) and examining perceived responsibility (Erlandsson et al., 2015).

targets.title: The "identified victim" effect: an identified group, or just a single individual?
targets.evidence_quote: We sought to revisit this classic finding and re-examine the conditions which encourage or discourage helping intention. We report an independent close replication of the identified single victim effect demonstrated in Kogut and Ritov (2005a) Study 2 along with two extensions, testing the effect of group belonging as a conceptual replication of Kogut and Ritov (2007) and examining perceived responsibility (Erlandsson et al., 2015).
targets.outcome_quote: Overall, our findings failed to find support for the findings by Kogut and Ritov (2005a) on the interaction between identifiability and singularity.

targets.title: "One of us": Outstanding willingness to help save a single identified compatriot
targets.evidence_quote: We sought to revisit this classic finding and re-examine the conditions which encourage or discourage helping intention. We report an independent close replication of the identified single victim effect demonstrated in Kogut and Ritov (2005a) Study 2 along with two extensions, testing the effect of group belonging as a conceptual replication of Kogut and Ritov (2007) and examining perceived responsibility (Erlandsson et al., 2015).
targets.outcome_quote: In our extension, we failed to find support for the findings by Kogut and Ritov (2007) that there is a higher likelihood of helping single victims over a group if they belong to the ingroup (vs. the outgroup).
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit author verdict on the target effect.
